questions.question: $P(x)$ is a degree 4 polynomial with real coefficients. Which statement must be false?
options: $P(x)=0$ has one repeated real root and two non-real roots
$P(x)=0$ has one real root and three non-real roots
questions.answer: **C.** Non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs.

questions.question: The points $z$, $iz$ and $z+iz$ ($z\ne0$) form a triangle. What is its area?
questions.answer: **B.** It is a right isosceles triangle with legs $|z|$.

questions.question: Which is an antiderivative of $\dfrac1{x\ln2x}$?
A 5 kg mass has velocity $\mathbf v(t)=3\sin2t\,\mathbf i+4\cos2t\,\mathbf j$ m/s. What is the maximum magnitude (N) of the net force on it?
questions.answer: **B.** $\mathbf a=6\cos2t\,\mathbf i-8\sin2t\,\mathbf j$ has maximum magnitude 8, so $F=40$.

questions.question: A particle has $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=-0.05(v^2-5)$. Its velocity falls from 50 m/s to 3 m/s. Which gives the time taken?
A particle in simple harmonic motion has $v^2=4-(x+1)^2$. Initially it is 1 m left of $O$ moving right at 2 m/s. Which could be its acceleration?
A particle moves with $x=3\cos nt$ and passes through the origin with speed $\sqrt3$ m/s. What is its period in seconds?
A particle of mass $m$ falls from rest with resistance of magnitude $\frac1{40}mv^2$ ($g=9.8$). What is its terminal velocity?
If $\text{Arg}\left(1-\dfrac1z\right)=\dfrac\pi3$, which is true?
questions.answer: **C.** The triangle with vertices $0,1,z$ has angle $\frac\pi3$ at $z$; apply the cosine rule.

questions.question: Which graph (A–D) best represents the complex numbers with $\text{Arg}\,z=|z|$?
questions.answer: **A.** $r=\theta$ with $0<\theta\le\pi$: a spiral from the origin to $(-\pi,0)$.

questions.question: Let $u=2\left(\cos\frac\pi{10}-i\sin\frac\pi{10}\right)$ and $v=\sqrt3-i$. Express $uv$ in modulus–argument form.
If $w^2=\sqrt3-i$, find all values of $w$.
Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_1^2x^2\sqrt{2-x}\,dx$.
The equation $iz^4+(-3-7i)z^3+(21+17i)z^2+(-51-15i)z+45=0$ has distinct roots $z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4$ (points $A,B,C,D$), with $z_1=-3i$, $z_3=3$ and $\text{Im}(z_4)>0$. Find $z_2$ and $z_4$.
questions.answer: Sum of roots $=7-3i$ gives $z_2+z_4=4$. Product $=\frac{45}i$ gives $z_2z_4=5$. So the roots of $x^2-4x+5=0$: $z_4=2+i$, $z_2=2-i$.

questions.question: $A=-3i$, $B=2-i$, $D=2+i$. The point $E$ representing $3w$ makes $ABDE$ a parallelogram. Find $w$ in modulus–argument form.
Sketch on an Argand diagram the region $1\le|z+2i|\le2$ and $\left|\arg(z+4i)-\dfrac{3\pi}8\right|\le\dfrac\pi8$.
questions.answer: The part of the annulus centred $(0,-2)$ with radii 1 and 2 lying between the rays from $(0,-4)$ at angles $\frac\pi4$ and $\frac\pi2$ (shaded, boundaries included).

questions.question: Express $\dfrac{3x+7}{(x+1)(x+2)(x+3)}$ in partial fractions.
Prove that $\displaystyle\int_0^1\dfrac{3x+7}{(x+1)(x+2)(x+3)}\,dx=\ln2$.
If $\omega$ is a non-real root of $z^3=1$, show that $\dfrac{\omega^2}{1+\omega^2}=-\dfrac1{\omega^2}$.

A loaded device of mass $m$ kg is dropped from a fixed height. It falls with negligible air resistance until a parachute opens after $\frac1{3k}$ s, after which there is resistance $mkv$ N ($v$ = speed, $k>0$). It lands with speed $\frac{5g}{6k}$ m/s. Show that its speed at $t=\frac1{3k}$ is $\frac g{3k}$.

A loaded device of mass $m$ kg is dropped from a fixed height. It falls with negligible air resistance until a parachute opens after $\frac1{3k}$ s, after which there is resistance $mkv$ N ($v$ = speed, $k>0$). It lands with speed $\frac{5g}{6k}$ m/s. The speed at $t=\frac1{3k}$ is $\frac g{3k}$. Show that for $t\ge\frac1{3k}$, $v=\dfrac gk\left(1-\dfrac23e^{\frac13-kt}\right)$.
questions.answer:
Downwards positive: $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=g-kv$, so $g-kv=Ae^{-kt}$.

At $t=\frac1{3k}$, $v=\frac g{3k}$: $A=\frac{2g}3e^{1/3}$. Rearranging gives $v=\dfrac gk\left(1-\dfrac23e^{\frac13-kt}\right)$.

questions.question: A loaded device of mass $m$ kg is dropped from a fixed height. It falls with negligible air resistance until a parachute opens after $\frac1{3k}$ s, after which there is resistance $mkv$ N ($v$ = speed, $k>0$). It lands with speed $\frac{5g}{6k}$ m/s. After the parachute opens, $v=\frac gk\left(1-\frac23e^{\frac13-kt}\right)$. Find the total time to reach the ground in terms of $k$.
A particle has acceleration $a=-5e^v$ and starts at the origin with velocity 2 m/s. Show that it comes to rest when $t=\frac15(1-e^{-2})$.
A particle has acceleration $a=-5e^v$ and starts at the origin with velocity 2 m/s. Show that it comes to rest at $x=\frac15(1-3e^{-2})$.
A particle has acceleration $a=-5e^v$ and starts at the origin with velocity 2 m/s. It comes to rest at $x=\frac15(1-3e^{-2})$ when $t=\frac15(1-e^{-2})$. Describe the motion.
questions.answer: It moves in the positive direction, slowing until it stops momentarily at that point. Since $a<0$ always, it then moves back in the negative direction with increasing speed.

questions.question: $u_1=\frac14$ and $u_{n+1}=u_n+\dfrac1{n(n+1)}+2^{-n}$ for $n\ge1$. Prove by induction that $u_n=\dfrac94-\dfrac1n-2^{1-n}$.
questions.answer:
$n=1$: $\frac94-1-1=\frac14$. Assume true for $n=k$:

$u_{k+1}=\frac94-\frac1k-2^{1-k}+\frac1k-\frac1{k+1}+2^{-k}=\frac94-\frac1{k+1}-2^{-k}$.

So the result holds for all $n\ge1$.

questions.question: Given $u_n=\frac94-\frac1n-2^{1-n}$ for positive integers $n$, show that $u_n<\frac94$.
Show that $v^2=n^2(A^2-x^2)$ satisfies $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=-n^2x$.
A particle with $\ddot x=-n^2x$ ($n>0$) starts at the origin. Find the first time its speed is half its maximum.
questions.answer: $x=A\sin nt$, $\dot x=An\cos nt$, maximum speed $|A|n$. $|\cos nt|=\frac12$ first when $t=\dfrac\pi{3n}$.

questions.question: A particle is projected from the origin at speed $V$ at $45^\circ$: $\mathbf r(t)=\left(\frac{Vt}{\sqrt2},\ \frac{Vt}{\sqrt2}-\frac12gt^2\right)$. Show that the trajectory is $y=x-\dfrac g{V^2}x^2$.

A particle is projected from the origin at speed $V$ at $45^\circ$: $\mathbf r(t)=\left(\frac{Vt}{\sqrt2},\ \frac{Vt}{\sqrt2}-\frac12gt^2\right)$. The path is $y=x-\frac{g}{V^2}x^2$. The roof of a barn is $y=x\tan\alpha+b$ ($b>0$, $\alpha$ acute). Show that if the particle just touches the roof, $V(\tan\alpha-1)=-2\sqrt{bg}$.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac g{V^2}x^2+(\tan\alpha-1)x+b=0$ has a double root: $(\tan\alpha-1)^2=\dfrac{4bg}{V^2}$.

The point of contact has $x=\dfrac{(1-\tan\alpha)V^2}{2g}>0$, so $\tan\alpha<1$ and $V(\tan\alpha-1)=-2\sqrt{bg}$.

questions.question: A particle is projected from the origin at speed $V$ at $45^\circ$: $\mathbf r(t)=\left(\frac{Vt}{\sqrt2},\ \frac{Vt}{\sqrt2}-\frac12gt^2\right)$. The path is $y=x-\frac{g}{V^2}x^2$. The roof of a barn is $y=x\tan\alpha+b$ ($b>0$, $\alpha$ acute). Given it just touches the roof, find the time of contact in terms of $\alpha$, $V$ and $g$.

A shape $ABCD$ is an equilateral triangle of side $2^n$ with an equilateral triangle of side 1 removed from one corner. A trapezium tile consists of three unit equilateral triangles. Prove by induction that the tiles can cover the shape without overlap for all positive integers $n$.
questions.answer:
$n=1$: the shape is exactly one tile.

Assume the shape of side $2^k$ can be tiled. Divide the shape of side $2^{k+1}$ into four triangles of side $2^k$. The top one already lacks its corner. Place one tile at the centre of the large triangle's base so that it covers one corner unit triangle from each of the other three (the two bottom triangles and the central one).

Each of the four pieces is now a copy of the side-$2^k$ shape, which can be tiled. So the result holds for $k+1$, and for all $n$.

questions.question: A shape $ABCD$ is an equilateral triangle of side $2^n$ with an equilateral triangle of side 1 removed from one corner. A trapezium tile consists of three unit equilateral triangles. Every such shape can be tiled. Explain why a regular hexagon of side $2^n$ can be tiled and find the number of tiles in terms of $n$.
questions.answer:
The hexagon is six equilateral triangles of side $2^n$ meeting at the centre. Remove from each the unit corner at the centre: each is then a tileable shape, and the six unit triangles left form a unit hexagon, covered by 2 tiles.

Total unit triangles $=6\times4^n$, so the number of tiles is $\dfrac{6\times4^n}3=2\times4^n=2^{2n+1}$.

questions.question: $OACB$ is a parallelogram with $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$. $M$ is on $OA$ with $OM=\frac15OA$, and $P$ is on $MB$ with $MP=\frac16MB$. Show that $P$ lies on $OC$.
questions.answer: $\overrightarrow{OP}=\frac15\mathbf a+\frac16\left(\mathbf b-\frac15\mathbf a\right)=\frac16(\mathbf a+\mathbf b)=\frac16\overrightarrow{OC}$, so $O,P,C$ are collinear.

questions.question: $OACB$ is a parallelogram with $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$. $M$ is on $OA$ with $OM=\frac15OA$, and $P$ is on $MB$ with $MP=\frac16MB$. State the ratio $OP:PC$.
A hose at the origin sprays water at speed $u$ at angle $\theta$, reaching a height of 80 m. With no air resistance, $\mathbf r=(ut\cos\theta,\ -5t^2+ut\sin\theta)$. Show that $u\sin\theta=40$.
Water leaves the origin at speed $u$ at angle $\theta$ with acceleration $(-0.2\dot x,\ -10-0.2\dot y)$. Show that $y=-5(50+u\sin\theta)e^{-0.2t}-50t+5(50+u\sin\theta)$.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac{d\dot y}{dt}=-\dfrac{50+\dot y}5$, with $\dot y(0)=u\sin\theta$, gives $\dot y=(50+u\sin\theta)e^{-0.2t}-50$.

Integrating with $y(0)=0$: $y=-5(50+u\sin\theta)e^{-0.2t}-50t+5(50+u\sin\theta)$.

questions.question: Water leaves the origin at speed $u$ at angle $\theta$ with acceleration $(-0.2\dot x,\ -10-0.2\dot y)$. Here $\dot y=(50+u\sin\theta)e^{-0.2t}-50$ and $y=-5(50+u\sin\theta)e^{-0.2t}-50t+5(50+u\sin\theta)$. Show that $y=5\left[-\dot y+u\sin\theta+50\ln\left(\dfrac{10+0.2\dot y}{10+0.2u\sin\theta}\right)\right]$.
questions.answer:
$(50+u\sin\theta)e^{-0.2t}=\dot y+50$, so $y=5(-\dot y+u\sin\theta-10t)$.

Also $t=-5\ln\dfrac{50+\dot y}{50+u\sin\theta}=-5\ln\dfrac{10+0.2\dot y}{10+0.2u\sin\theta}$.

Substituting gives the result.

questions.question: Water leaves the origin at speed $u$ at angle $\theta$ with acceleration $(-0.2\dot x,\ -10-0.2\dot y)$. Given $u\sin\theta=40$ and $y=5\left[-\dot y+u\sin\theta+50\ln\left(\frac{10+0.2\dot y}{10+0.2u\sin\theta}\right)\right]$, how high does the water reach, to the nearest metre?
$f$ and $g$ are continuous on $[0,a]$ with $f(x)=f(a-x)$ and $g(x)+g(a-x)=m$. Show that $\displaystyle\int_0^af(x)g(x)\,dx=\frac m2\int_0^af(x)\,dx$.
Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^\pi x\sin x\cos^4x\,dx$.
Let $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^1(1-x)^ne^x\,dx$, $n$ a non-negative integer. Show that $I_n=-1+nI_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$.
Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^1(1-x)^3e^x\,dx$.
Prove that $\displaystyle\int_0^af(a-x)\,dx=\int_0^af(x)\,dx$.
Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}x|\cos x|\,dx$.
For integer $n\ge2$, prove that $\sin\dfrac\pi{2n}\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sin\dfrac{k\pi}n=\cos\dfrac\pi{2n}$.

Let $\alpha=\cos\dfrac{2\pi}n+i\sin\dfrac{2\pi}n$ ($n\ge2$). Using $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sin\frac{k\pi}n=\cot\frac\pi{2n}$, prove that $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}|\alpha^k-1|=2\cot\dfrac\pi{2n}$.
questions.answer:
$\alpha^k-1=\cos\frac{2k\pi}n-1+i\sin\frac{2k\pi}n=2i\sin\frac{k\pi}n\left(\cos\frac{k\pi}n+i\sin\frac{k\pi}n\right)$.

Since $\sin\frac{k\pi}n>0$ for $1\le k\le n-1$, $|\alpha^k-1|=2\sin\frac{k\pi}n$. Summing gives $2\cot\frac\pi{2n}$.
